hits.name: levelsio
hits.text: I take 10g per day!
hits.hook: I take 10g per day!
hits.quote_note: quotes a thread about a new creatine study
hits.draft_en:
Five words. 518k views.

Pieter quoted a creatine study and added: I take 10g per day.

The study claim was big. The Community Note was bigger: the gain was lean mass that includes water, muscle growth was not measured, and lifting vs not lifting was not randomized.

AI news works the same way. The headline travels on a one-line endorsement. The fine print travels in the notes.

Before you quote a benchmark, read the method. Post the caveat with the claim and you earn the trust the hype accounts lose.
hits.video_tip: 8-10s: headline card 'creatine beats lifting', a Community Note slides over it, caption read the method before you quote.

Ask your agent which models your current machine can run. Install one tonight.

hits.name: levelsio
hits.text:
Airbnb just responded to "reviewgate"

The replies here are literally hundreds of people who got their reviews removed directly contradicting what Airbnb says here

The "policy" they have seems to be to remove a guest's review and rating whenever a host asks for it

I don't get why they don't just fix this? Everyone would love to see Airbnb have honest reviews and ratings you can trust

Short term you might get more bookings if everything is a 4.5 or 4.99 but long term people discover it means nothing and they can't trust your platform and they leave elsewhere

I think they're in some internal gridlock by MBAs who want to see revenue go up, not realizing that they're destroying a company

I hope they fix it!
hits.hook: Airbnb just responded to "reviewgate"  The replies here are literally hundreds of people who got their reviews removed d
hits.quote_note: quotes @airbnbhelp saying it removes reviews that violate its policies
hits.draft_en:
Airbnb answered "reviewgate" and the replies did the fact check.

Hundreds of people say their reviews were removed after a host asked. Pieter's read: short term, a 4.99 everywhere sells more nights. Long term, people learn the number means nothing and leave.

That trade shows up in every product with a score: app store ratings, AI eval dashboards, NPS.

If users can see the gap between your number and their experience, the number is now a liability.

Audit what gets removed from your reviews this week, and publish the rule.
hits.video_tip: 10s: official statement card, then a flood of reply bubbles saying 'mine got removed', caption the replies are the fact check.

hits.text:
I'm not paid by the hotel lobby or something btw

I was a big fan of Airbnb and would prefer to stay in Airbnbs if they were great

I want to have a kitchen to cook steak and vegetables, and not go outside to eat in restaurants or get shitty hotel food

But I can't book Airbnbs because I the "rating anxiety" is so high because I can't trust the ratings and I end up with my bags in some place that sucks, so the variation of quality is too high to be able to seriously use for travel  (except maybe in Asia)

So they leave us no choice to just go back to hotels

Meanwhile hotels still don't have kitchens! What a missed opportunity! Hotel industry could CLEAN UP entire Airbnb by just adding kitchens to rooms
hits.hook: I'm not paid by the hotel lobby or something btw  I was a big fan of Airbnb and would prefer to stay in Airbnbs if they
hits.quote_note: quotes own post: Imagine choosing an Airbnb over a hotel
hits.draft_en:
Pieter wants to stay in Airbnbs. He books hotels anyway.

The reason is rating anxiety. When every listing says 4.9, you cannot tell good from bad, so you pick the option you can predict.

His fix for hotels: add kitchens to rooms and clean up Airbnb's whole market.

That is the opening when a platform loses trust. The incumbent does not have to be better. It has to be predictable plus one missing feature.

Find the competitor your users stopped trusting. Ship the one thing they still go there for.

virals.angle: Your rating is lying, and your users know
virals.draft_en:
Airbnb says hosts cannot delete reviews. Hundreds of replies say theirs got removed anyway.

There are YouTube guides ranking the best excuse to get a review taken down. Discrimination and extortion: very high odds.

So every listing says 4.99, nobody trusts it, and Pieter books hotels instead.

AI products are walking into the same trap. Every dashboard says the agent did great. Every eval is green.

A score users cannot trust is worse than no score.

Pick the one number your users rely on. Show the bad results too. That is the feature.
virals.video_tip: 10-12s: 4.99 rating card cracking as reply bubbles pour in, then an honest histogram, caption a score you can't trust is worse than none.

virals.inspired_by: @AlexFinn Beam (217k) + @MishaLaskin Beam launch (71k) + @nutlope Together Link (7k) + Agr open decision model (25k)
virals.draft_en:
The open-weights race got a new player this week.

Reflection's Beam: 500B parameters, 23B active, weights out this month. Together Link routes open models into Claude Code, Codex and opencode. Command Code shipped Agr, a small open model just for tool calls and routing.

Put those together and the stack writes itself: a big open model for hard tasks, a tiny one for routing, your harness on top.

No rate limits. No surprise bill.

This week, run one real coding task on an open model and write down the cost and the result.
virals.video_tip: 12s: cloud logo shrinking into a desktop tower, router arrows splitting tasks between big and tiny models, caption your own frontier stack.

virals.angle: Agents need a memory and a name tag
virals.inspired_by: @cognition Dreaming (481k) + @nikitabier agent identity standard (450k) + @SoniaBaschez AI wife (198k)
virals.draft_en:
The two biggest agent posts this week were not about smarter models.

Cognition's Devin now builds a memory of how you work and cleans it up overnight. Nikita Bier says the most important problem of the next five years is a standard for agents to identify themselves to services.

And Sonia Baschez nailed what users want: not an agent that books a flight, but one that knows your whole life and runs it.

Memory makes agents useful. Identity makes them welcome.

If you build agents, ship both before you ship another benchmark.
virals.video_tip: 10s: an agent avatar gaining a memory card and then a name badge at a website door, caption memory plus identity.

virals.inspired_by: @AlexFinn Meta Muse (65k) + @tdinh_me Cursor cloud agent QA (7k) + @craigweiss agent-booked trip (28k)
virals.draft_en:
The best agent posts this week showed a chore vanishing.

Alex Finn has every task he hates on Meta Muse. Tony Dinh's PRs now come with screenshots and video demos from a cloud agent.

And Craig Weiss showed the flip side: an agent booked his whole trip, including a 6-day layover in Cleveland and a one-way ticket to Newark.

Both posts work for the same reason. A concrete before and after.

Pick one chore. Hand it to an agent. Post the minutes saved, or the funniest way it went wrong.
virals.video_tip: 10-14s: chore checklist ticking off on its own, then a glitchy itinerary 'Cleveland 6 days' stamp, caption post the before and after.

virals.angle: AI money is a service business
virals.inspired_by: @0xCodila $500 AI videos (401k) + @Stringcodes Macbook + Claude $1M (152k) + @tdinh_me AI-hires-humans agency (10k)
virals.draft_en:
"Just got a Macbook and a Claude subscription. How do I make $1M?" pulled 150k views.

The real answers were sitting in the same feed. Companies pay about $500 for 15-second AI videos. Tony Dinh saw a tool that lets AI hire people to post, and his first thought was an agency.

The money is not in using AI. It is in selling the output to people who never will.

One skill, one offer, one buyer type.

Write your offer in one line today: I make X for Y using AI, delivered in Z days.
virals.video_tip: 10s: laptop plus Claude logo, then an invoice card '$500 per 15s video' stamping in, caption sell the output, not the tool.
